name: How much contingency should you keep for a custom home in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should you keep for a custom home in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should you keep for a custom home in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A custom home in Los Angeles should usually include a contingency reserve of at least 10% to 20%, with higher reserves for hillside lots, older tear-downs, or highly customized architecture. Contingency exists because even well-planned projects can uncover soil issues, utility conflicts, hidden structural problems, or permit-driven changes. It also covers homeowner decisions made after construction starts, which can be expensive once trades are scheduled and materials are ordered. The most practical way to use contingency is to treat it as a protected reserve rather than extra spending money. Homeowners should ask the builder what risks are already included in the base estimate and what could still trigger added cost. If the project has steep slopes, demolition, or extensive site work, a larger reserve provides much-needed flexibility. Underfunded contingency is one of the main reasons custom home projects become stressful. A realistic budget is always safer than a perfect-looking budget with no margin.
